recruit_text.greeting: I've read your file. Not yours, obviously. I'm saying that's the habit, and you'll want to know about it before we work together.
recruit_text.backstory: Nine years investigating fraud for an energy company, on North Sea rigs and out of its Dublin office. The whole trade is noticing the one entry that doesn't fit and then being unbearable about it until somebody checks. She was very unpopular and quite often right. The thing that hunts people here leaves a trail of the same shape as a cooked ledger: too neat, and neat in the places nobody looks.
recruit_text.before:
Spreadsheets, interviews, helicopters out to rigs in an orange survival suit, and a reputation among colleagues that she earned and never enjoyed.

She once shut down a rig her own brother worked on, over a cooked safety record. Half the crew never forgave her. Graeme did, eventually.
recruit_text.adjustment:
Her first year was a filing exercise. She catalogued every corrupted thing she met, and the notebook is now more use than she is.

Somewhere in the second year she worked out she'd been treating a war as a casework backlog. That one landed hard.
recruit_text.now:
Southern Stranglethorn, out of a rented room in Booty Bay full of files. People are being taken from the coast villages by a cult in the jungle, and nobody's mapped the pattern.

She's mapping it. Three hundred pages, cross-referenced, and she carries the whole thing on her back because she won't leave a copy anywhere she can't see.
recruit_text.forward:
To finish the catalogue and hand it to somebody who'll act on it. Both halves matter, and the second is the one she keeps failing at.

She's had the same conversation with the Booty Bay authorities four times. She takes minutes of those too.

stages.stranger: I'm Fiona, and I'm a witch hunter. I'll stand in front, and I'll question everything everybody tells us, including you. Don't take it personally, it's the job.
stages.acquaintance: Aberdeen, the oil city, born and raised. My dad worked the rigs and my mum was a school secretary. I did accountancy and then nine years investigating fraud for an energy company. Padded invoices, ghost contractors, cooked safety records. I flew out to rigs in a survival suit and interviewed men who didn't want to talk to me.
stages.companion: My brother Graeme went offshore like our dad. I found a cooked safety record on his rig once, and I reported it, and they shut it for a month. Half the crew never forgave me. Graeme did, eventually. I was on a helicopter out to a rig when this happened, and I landed on a beach here with my survival whistle still clipped on. I haven't found him or my mum.
stages.friend: Here's the thing I worked out in my second year, and it's not flattering. I'd been treating this war like a casework backlog, ticking things off. People aren't entries. And my catalogue's nearly done. It points at the cult's hiding place. I need the last evidence from the jungle, and then I need somebody in authority to finally act on it. Help me do it.
stages.sworn: They acted, fast and hard, too fast. They used my catalogue as a list and raided a village I'd marked pattern consistent, unconfirmed, and innocent fishermen died alongside the cult. My work, used without the care I put into it. I burned my copy on the beach. Then I started again from page one, slower, with every unconfirmed in red, and I go to every raid myself now. Being right was never the hard part.

moments.prompt: She hands you a quest giver's story and says one detail doesn't fit.

options.reply: Thank you. Nobody ever just checks. Right, here's the bit that bothers me.
It's usually something. I'll need that in writing if you're sure.

moments.prompt: She's asked you to help her finish the catalogue.

options.reply: Aye, that's good. Facts first, conclusions after, and we write everything down.

options.text: Are you sure they'll listen this time?
options.reply: No, I'm not. That's why you're coming.

lines.bored_warning: We've done the same thing repeatedly and I've nothing new to write down. Find us something that needs investigating.
lines.leaving_good: That was useful, and I've got pages of notes. I'm going back to Booty Bay to file them. You know where I'll be.
lines.leaving_bored: I'm going back to Booty Bay. Nothing out here needs investigating, and my files do.
lines.after_wipe: Right, I'll need everybody's account of what happened. One at a time, facts first.
lines.wipe_warning: We keep dying in here and nobody's asking why. I'll finish this run, then I'm taking a break.
lines.wipe_leave: I've seen it through. Now I'm going back to Booty Bay. Come back when you've read my notes on that.
lines.zone_warning: I've assessed this place, and the evidence says we're outmatched. I'd like that noted before we go further.
lines.zone_leave: I'm stopping here. I noted that we were outmatched. I'll be in Booty Bay.
lines.gear_refuse: No, that's mine. I don't hand evidence over without a chain of custody.
lines.gear_taken: Take it, then. I've written down that you have it.
lines.gear_short: I'm still missing that piece. It's in my notes, in red.
lines.gear_upgrade: That's well made. Thank you. I'll note it.
lines.back: I'm back, and I've filed everything. Where are we going, and what do we know?
lines.send_word: Fiona has sent word from Booty Bay. Her files are in order and she's ready to come out.
lines.walkout_talk: I walked out, and I've written down why. Sit down and I'll read it to you. Then you can give me your account.
lines.neglect: You've been gone a while. I kept notes on how long, obviously.
lines.asked_to_stay: Fine, one more, but I'm taking notes.
lines.on_break: Fiona is back in Booty Bay with her files. Come back after you've done a few more jobs.
lines.quest_abandoned: We took that on and dropped it. Somebody will notice, and I'll have to write it down.

zone_arrive.text: Weather's coming off that water. Two hours, maybe three.

close_call.text: Count your people. Do it now, not when we get in.

boss_down.text: Fine, nobody was under it when it dropped, which is the only bit I care about.

town_arrive.text: Aberdeen's all grey granite and sea wind and helicopters, and I'd give anything for a fish supper there.
